title: The Mountain Collision That Cooled Our Planet
description: Discover how the tectonic collision that formed the Himalayas acted as a giant geological thermostat, pulling carbon from the atmosphere and plunging Earth into the ice ages.
instagram_caption: Fifty million years ago, a massive continental collision did more than build the tallest peaks on Earth—it completely rewrote our global climate. 🏔️❄️ Here is how the Himalayas cooled down a tropical planet. #EarthHistory #Geology #ClimateChange #Himalayas #ScienceFacts

segments.narration: Fifty million years ago, a colossal land collision began rewriting the climate of our entire planet.
Before these peaks rose, Earth was a tropical hothouse—until the Indian plate rammed into Asia, lifting the giant Himalayas.
Violent monsoon rains washed over this new rock, combining with atmospheric carbon dioxide and locking the greenhouse gas safely in the oceans.
broll_queries: heavy monsoon rain falling on rocks

segments.narration: This massive geological sponge stripped carbon from the sky, dragging Earth out of its warm state and triggering the modern ice ages.
Every time you look at these snow-capped peaks, you are seeing the ancient thermostat that cooled our world.
